classification.difficultyReason: Interpret stepped and sloping solids and draw their visible edges in three orthographic views.

content.prompt: Draw the front view, side view and plan view.

spec.description: Broad low base with a taller central block, low shoulders, a labelled front stepped face and labelled right side. Decorative blue outlines become black.
spec.mathematics: Uniform-depth stepped prism; two equal-height shoulders flank the raised central section. No numerical dimensions are given.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the supplied solid and viewing labels are visible.

answer.short: Front: a raised central rectangle with lower shoulders. Side: a rectangle with a horizontal line halfway up. Plan: a rectangle divided into a narrow strip, a broad central strip and a narrow strip.
answer.worked: Look directly towards the face labelled front to obtain the stepped outline. From the labelled side, the lower shoulder hides the bottom half of the central block, leaving a horizontal visible edge. From above, draw the rectangular footprint and the two boundaries of the raised central strip.

spec.description: Three labelled orthographic drawings with visible internal edges.
spec.mathematics: Stepped front, horizontally divided side rectangle and three-strip plan.

spec.description: Prism with a short horizontal raised top followed by a descending slope; long profile labelled side and low right end labelled front.
spec.mathematics: Constant width; raised horizontal section joins a sloping section ending above the base.
spec.answerVisibility: No orthographic answers appear in the question.

answer.short: Front: a rectangle with a horizontal line near the bottom. Side: a profile with a short horizontal top followed by a downward slope. Plan: a rectangle with one transverse dividing line.
answer.worked: The front view includes the low front edge and the higher rear portion visible above it. The side view retains the horizontal top section and its descending slope. The plan shows the rectangular footprint and the boundary where the horizontal top meets the slope.

spec.description: Front rectangle with low horizontal edge, sloping side profile and divided rectangular plan.
spec.mathematics: The top break is visible in plan; the low end edge is visible in front elevation.

spec.description: Three-level stair solid with two narrow lower treads and a broad top platform; front is the low near end and side is the stepped-profile side.
spec.mathematics: Three equal vertical rises; two short treads precede a longer top platform. Constant transverse width.

answer.short: Front: a rectangle divided into three horizontal bands. Side: a three-level staircase rising to a broad top platform. Plan: a rectangle divided into two narrow strips and one broad strip.
answer.worked: From the front, the three risers appear as horizontal bands across the full width. From the side, retain the complete staircase outline, including the longer upper platform. From above, the footprint is rectangular and the two changes of level appear as transverse lines.

spec.description: Three orthographic views showing all three levels and the broad upper platform.
spec.mathematics: Three-band front, staircase side, and two narrow strips followed by a broad strip in plan.

spec.description: Three raised transverse ridges separated by two rectangular channels; long notched side and rectangular front end are labelled.
spec.mathematics: Five longitudinal strips alternate ridge, channel, ridge, channel, ridge; channels have equal depth above a continuous base.

answer.short: Front: a rectangle. Side: a rectangular profile with two rectangular notches in its top edge. Plan: a rectangle divided into five strips.
answer.worked: The nearest ridge hides the channels in the front view, giving a rectangle. Looking directly at the labelled side reveals all three ridges and both channels. From above, draw the rectangular footprint with four transverse boundaries separating the five alternating strips.

spec.description: Rectangular front, two-notched side and five-strip plan.
spec.mathematics: Three ridges and two channels; front ridge occludes the remaining structure in front elevation.
